Preparation Tips
Fresh pork was once cooked to an internal
temperature of 170° to 185° Fahrenheit to
avoid trichinosis.  But with the new lean-
er pork, such a temperature is no longer
necessary, nor is it advised.  Cooking meat
to this temperature will dry out the pork,
making it chewy and hard to cut.  Some
older cookbooks on your shelf still may
advise this higher temperature as a guide,
but a better internal temperature is 160°
to 170° Fahrenheit, which will produce
juicy, tender meat.  At this temperature,
the inside of a fresh pork cut may still be
pinkish.  This tinge of color is nothing to
worry about as long as the internal tem-
perature has reached at least 160°.  That
temperature destroys any organisms that
could cause trichinosis. 
Fresh cuts of pork can be prepared with
dry-heat cooking methods of grilling, broil-
ing, and roasting, but marinating or basting
may be necessary to keep the meat tender.
Fresh pork cooked to an internal
temperature of 160° Fahrenheit
